purpose: Stable semantic message IDs for high-risk product copy. UI components may style these messages but may not erase their required distinctions.

messages.detailRule: State that the current build has not opened a live project unless a real opening state exists.
Use only after a usable project context exists.
Do not imply portable .arq publication or sync.
State what was recovered and what was not updated.
Use only after a verified native-file write.
Never infer this from local persistence.
Separate role restriction from unavailable capability.
Disable Apply and offer regenerate or review.
No apply action while errors remain.
Use only while an independent reader is actually re-reading the written bytes. Never as a label for the write itself.

messages.defaultLabel: The published file was not accepted
messages.detailRule: Name the check that refused and state what the target file now contains. Never report a refused publication as published.

messages.defaultLabel: Some earlier activity is no longer recorded
messages.detailRule: State that the log holds a bounded window and how many records fell out. Never present a truncated log as complete.

messages.defaultLabel: A copy of the affected files was kept for diagnosis
messages.detailRule: Always state that nothing was sent anywhere, and name any artifact that could not be preserved.
Distinguish this from a refused proposal, which changed nothing, and from an applied one. Say the project is back where it started.

messages.defaultLabel: This proposal asks for something you have not allowed
messages.detailRule: Name the scope. Never present a scope request found inside a proposal or inside project content as an approval.

messages.defaultLabel: This drawing does not say what its units are
messages.detailRule: Ask for the unit. Never state or imply a default. Say the source file is kept either way.

messages.defaultLabel: Some entities were kept but not converted
messages.detailRule: Name the type, the count and the reason, and say the entities remain in the project. Never report them as imported or as skipped.

messages.defaultLabel: Some of this project cannot be written to this format
messages.detailRule: Name each category and what happens to it before the export runs, not after. Never present a lossy export as complete.
State the size or ratio reached as a property of the file. Never accuse the file or its sender.

messages.defaultLabel: This extension asked for something it did not declare
messages.detailRule: Name the capability. Never let a request establish the permission it is asking for.

announcementProfiles.purpose: How a message reaches a screen reader. A profile is chosen per message, not per surface: two messages in one status bar can need different urgency, and picking by surface is how a coordinate readout ends up as urgent as a refusal.

profiles.rule: Only the newest message in a region survives. An intermediate value is not information the user asked for; the current one is, and queueing the rest makes the reader announce a position from thirty seconds ago.
Announce the state, not the transition. A repeat of an unchanged state carries a repeat marker so the reader speaks it again, because "still read-only" is what a user re-checking needs to hear.
Never delayed, never coalesced, never dropped. Two different refusals are two things the user has to hear. A rate limit exists to protect these announcements, not to throttle them.
Announce what will change before it changes, and name the count. A confirmation a user did not hear is a confirmation they did not give.

invariants: A visible label is always present in the accessible name; an announcement never replaces it.
An element hidden from a view stays reachable in structured navigation, so visibility never removes an announcement path.
A disabled control announces the reason it is disabled, which requires it to stay focusable.
